This page details the installation and usage of the C++ version of the PropLib implementation of the Low Frequency / Medium Frequency (IF77) propagation model.

{{< include /includes/_link_to_model_home.qmd >}}

## Installation

To use the C++ library in your code, you'll need to download the shared library (`.dll` on Windows, `.dylib` on macOS, or `.so` on Linux) and the header file. These are distributed for each supported platform as part of the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NTIA/IF77/releases/) starting with v1.1. Prior to v1.1, support was only provided for Windows platforms.

To use the shared library in your project, you'll need to link against it. The details for this process differ depending on your compiler and/or IDE, but generally you will need to somehow provide the path to the files you downloaded from the GitHub release.

Once you've linked the dynamic library to your project, all you need to do is include the appropriate header file and, optionally, use its namespace:

```cpp
#include "IF77.h"

using namespace ITS::Propagation::IF77;  // Optional: makes later code more concise
```

This library has no external C++ dependencies.

{{< include /includes/cpp/_documentation.qmd >}}

[Docs](https://ntia.github.io/if77){.btn .btn-secondary .btn role="button"}

## Examples

The following code example shows how the IF77 model can be called in a C++ program.

### Calling the IF77 Model

```cpp
#include "IF77.h"
using namespace ITS::Propagation::IF77;

int main() {
    // Define inputs
    double h_tx__meter = 0.0;   // Height of the transmitter
    double h_rx__meter = 0.0;   // Height of the receiver
    double f__mhz = 0.01;       // Frequency
    double P_tx__watt = 1000.0; // Transmitter power
    double N_s = 301.0;         // Surface refractivity
    double d__km = 1000.0;      // Path distance
    double epsilon = 15.0;      // Relative permittivity
    double sigma = 0.005;       // Conductivity
    Polarization pol = Polarization::HORIZONTAL;    // Polarization

    // Create struct to store outputs
    Result result;      // IF77 result structure
    ReturnCode rtn;     // Return code

    // Call the model
    rtn = IF77_CPP(h_tx__meter, h_rx__meter, f__mhz, P_tx__watt, N_s, d__km, epsilon, sigma, pol, &result);

    // rtn is 0 (SUCCESS)
    // result.A_btl__db is 184.49 dB
    // result.E_dBuVm is -82.50 dB(uV/m)
    // result.P_rx__dbm is -114.93 dBm
    // result.method is 1 (RESIDUE_SERIES)
}
```
